Above 10 bar, PR + gE (MHV1) is recommended here. PR at 7000 kPa, a light gas with a polar liquid (Carbon dioxide + Methanol, Carbon dioxide + Water, Hydrogen + Methanol, Hydrogen + Water, Carbon monoxide + Methanol, Carbon monoxide + Water, Nitrogen + Methanol, Nitrogen + Water): above about 10 bar the method guide recommends a cubic equation with a gE mixing rule (rule 4 of docs/METHOD_SELECTION.md). In CHEPTA that is "PR + gE (MHV1)" (model "PR", mixing: "MHV1"), which has NRTL parameters for these pairs: Carbon dioxide + Methanol: fitted inside the rule, with a fit-quality warning; Carbon dioxide + Water: fitted inside the rule, with a fit-quality warning; Hydrogen + Methanol: fitted inside the rule, with a fit-quality warning; Hydrogen + Water: fitted inside the rule; Carbon monoxide + Methanol: fitted inside the rule; Carbon monoxide + Water: fitted inside the rule, with a fit-quality warning; Nitrogen + Methanol: fitted inside the rule; Nitrogen + Water: fitted inside the rule, with a fit-quality warning. This calculation uses PR with k_ij.

Carbon monoxide: ideal-gas heat capacity at 521.11 K is 21.11 K above its range (68.16-500 K): the record's own equation is evaluated beyond its range (the Aly-Lee form, which follows the molecule's vibrational heat capacity). This is an extrapolation, not data.

PR is the method here: Carbon dioxide, Hydrogen, Carbon monoxide, Nitrogen are light gases, which only an equation of state describes (gas-phase reactors and high-pressure loops are simulated so). For a liquid of the polar components alone (Methanol, Water) below about 10 bar, such as their distillation, an activity model (NRTL or UNIQUAC) would be more accurate (docs/METHOD_SELECTION.md).

Above 10 bar, PR + gE (MHV1) is recommended here. PR at 3000 kPa, a light gas with a polar liquid (Carbon dioxide + Methanol, Carbon dioxide + Water, Hydrogen + Methanol, Hydrogen + Water, Carbon monoxide + Methanol, Carbon monoxide + Water, Nitrogen + Methanol, Nitrogen + Water): above about 10 bar the method guide recommends a cubic equation with a gE mixing rule (rule 4 of docs/METHOD_SELECTION.md). In CHEPTA that is "PR + gE (MHV1)" (model "PR", mixing: "MHV1"), which has NRTL parameters for these pairs: Carbon dioxide + Methanol: fitted inside the rule, with a fit-quality warning; Carbon dioxide + Water: fitted inside the rule, with a fit-quality warning; Hydrogen + Methanol: fitted inside the rule, with a fit-quality warning; Hydrogen + Water: fitted inside the rule; Carbon monoxide + Methanol: fitted inside the rule; Carbon monoxide + Water: fitted inside the rule, with a fit-quality warning; Nitrogen + Methanol: fitted inside the rule; Nitrogen + Water: fitted inside the rule, with a fit-quality warning. This calculation uses PR with k_ij.

PR is the method here: Carbon dioxide, Hydrogen, Carbon monoxide, Nitrogen are light gases, which only an equation of state describes (gas-phase reactors and high-pressure loops are simulated so). For a liquid of the polar components alone (Methanol, Water) below about 10 bar, such as their distillation, an activity model (NRTL or UNIQUAC) would be more accurate (docs/METHOD_SELECTION.md).
